proposals.evidence: DEDR3876 directly gives Tamil paṭṭai, Malayalam paṭṭa, Kannada paṭṭe and Telugu paṭṭa bark. Survey Tamil paṭṭe preserves its final-vowel difference. Badaga paṭṭe is a comparative extension explicitly only a look-alike in the source, with no claim that Badaga is listed in this article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5259 documents Malayalam vayaṟu and Toda pīṟ belly, along with Tamil vayiṟu and the wider vac-Vṯ family. Survey vayarə and pir correspond directly. Ravula bairu/bārə are comparative extensions labelled look-alikes in the source; their initial voicing and contraction remain visible for review. The number474 in the annotation is the page, not the two numeral article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR399 explicitly gives Tamil āṇ male and Malayalam āṇ male. Survey āṇ/āṇə man preserves its final vowel and elicited gloss. One upstream Tamil annotation incorrectly says no resembling form occurs; the complete article does list āṇ, so that negative claim is not repeated. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5535 gives Kodagu bērï, Malayalam vēr and Tamil vēr root. Survey bērə/vērə preserve their final vowels and match the same botanical sense; source cognacy independently identifies the article. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3633 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam nākku and Toda nōf tongue; survey nākkə/nākə and nōf preserve their spellings. Betta Kurumba nelgi is a comparative extension toward the nālage/nālige series documented in Kannada, explicitly only a look-alike in the source. This does not treat the Betta form as a literal DEDR attestation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
